title: FACT CHECK: Trump did not call an ABS-CBN reporter ‘stupid’
summary: In the video, the person US President Donald Trump addressed as ‘stupid’ was a reporter from ABC News, not ABS-CBN News

blocks.text: Claim: US President Donald Trump called a reporter from ABS-CBN News “stupid.”

Why we fact-checked this: The claim was made in a video posted by Facebook user Herson Capino on November 16. Though the reaction count was hidden, the post reached over 3,700 comments and 4,700 shares as of writing.
The video shows Trump entertaining questions from the media. After one reporter spoke to Trump, he asked: “Are you a stupid person?”
Trump then asked the reporter which news organization they were working for. He doubled down, again called the reporter “stupid” and added that their network is the “worst of all.”
Text overlaid on the video reads, “Isang reporter ng ABS-CBN tinawag ni President Donald Trump na ‘Are you stupid’.”
(President Donald Trump asked a reporter from ABS-CBN, ‘Are you stupid?’)
Several users have reposted the video, with some leaving comments saying the supposed ABS-CBN reporter was humiliated by the exchange.
The facts: Trump did not call an ABS-CBN reporter stupid. The US president was talking to a reporter from an American TV network, ABC News.

According to a fact-check by ABS-CBN News, the Facebook reel misrepresents an October 21, 2026 video, in which a reporter asked Trump whether the US waived sanctions on Russia in exchange for the release of Stephen Hubbard, an American jailed in Russia for allegedly fighting for Ukraine.
In the original clip, the reporter can be heard answering “ABC News” when asked to identify their news organization.
The misleading reels merely added overlaid text falsely claiming that Trump was speaking to a reporter from ABS-CBN.

Trump in PH: The posts circulated on social media as Trump arrived in Manila on November 17 for a state visit and to participate in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)-US Special Summit, as well as the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue leaders’ summit. (READ: Marcos rolls out red carpet for Trump state visit)

Following his bilateral meeting with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., Trump said on November 18 that the US and the Philippines secured a trade deal — the “biggest deal” so far between the two countries. However, he gave no details about the deal. Marcos’ office later said both sides reached an understanding on areas of economic cooperation.

The US president then headed to China for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, focusing on issues like nuclear weapons, trade, and tensions over Ukraine and Iran.
